Act as the test sub-agent for this task.

You are working in the Moneo repo (read AGENTS.md and `e2e/README.md` first and follow them exactly: no comments, surgical changes, QA backend only — never the owner's backend on port 3000 or `.env`; mock AI/bank/Scalable). Your checkout is based on the latest `main`. Create a branch `t3/audit-browser-suite`, commit each fix separately in plain language, push, and open ONE pull request to `main`. Do not merge it. Do not touch PR #313.

## Goal: make the Playwright suite green (the failures a QA audit found)

Set up QA if needed (`npm run setup -- --qa`, `npm run qa:auth`); `npm run test:e2e` starts the QA server itself. Reproduce each failure first, then fix the first place it goes wrong. Never delete or skip a failing test to get green — fix the cause, or report it.

1. **Full discovery breaks on `e2e/artifact-page-protection.mocked.spec.ts`.** It imports `artifactDocument`/`artifactFrameCsp` from `lib/ai/artifact-data.ts`, which pulls in Scalable live data and `lib/service-db.ts`, whose `import "server-only"` throws in the Playwright process. Fix at the source: move the pure HTML/CSP helpers into their own module with no server imports (in `lib/`, respecting `moneo/import-boundaries`), and have both the app and the spec import that. Confirm `npx playwright test --list` discovers every spec.
2. **`e2e/core-journey.smoke.spec.ts` "the setup page explains how to finish setup"** expects the "Moneo could not sign you in" screen, but its context is signed in, so `/setup` redirects to Overview. Run that test with a signed-out context (no storage state), and check `app/setup/page.tsx` to see what state shows that screen — set it up the way the real failed-sign-in path happens.
3. **`e2e/import-control.mocked.spec.ts`**: "a delayed poll cannot replace canceled status or its fresh counts", "…completed status…" (both waited 30 s for the intentionally delayed poll and never received it), and "a newer request with an older queued snapshot cannot regress running progress" (stayed queued after a mocked running response). Decide whether the app or the test is wrong: read the import page's polling code (`app/import/…`, `usePolling` in `lib/use-polling.ts`) — e.g. the app may no longer issue the poll the test waits for, or the route pattern no longer matches. If the app regresses stale-response handling, fix the app (that is a real bug: an old poll overwriting a newer status); if the test's mock is outdated, fix the test so it still proves the stale-response guard (break the guard locally and confirm the test fails).
4. **`e2e/home-dashboard.gated.spec.ts` "a long press drags a widget on a phone, and a swipe still scrolls"** is flaky on a reused QA user (scroll stayed at 415 for 5 s) and passes with a fresh user. Make the spec set up the state it needs (AGENTS.md: each spec sets up its own state) and find why existing state breaks the swipe — if it is an app bug (e.g. a drag state left armed), fix the app.
5. **`e2e/net-worth.gated.spec.ts`**: a selector expecting one Scalable deposit row matched two possibly-valid rows on a shared QA user. Make the spec's selector target the row it created (unique synthetic description/amount), not "the only Scalable deposit".

Out of scope: `import-control.gated.spec.ts` "durable import Stop, Resume…" (5,000-row import hitting a Postgres statement timeout) — that is a separate task; leave it as is and mention it in the PR.

## Checks
- Run each fixed spec at least 3 times (`--repeat-each=3`) and then the full suite once (`npm run test:e2e`, excluding paid provider specs as `e2e/README.md` describes); report pass counts.
- `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build` if you touched app code.
- Check the GitHub issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" (`gh issue list --search "Nightly browser suite"`) and mention in the PR which of its listed failures this fixes.
- PR description: per failure, the cause and the fix; a **Speed** section (skill `measure-speed`; if app code changed, measure the affected action; otherwise "No runtime change"). End commit messages with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` and the PR description with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- When finished, stop any servers you started and leave no temporary checkouts.

When done, your last line must be: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

t3/audit-browser-suite
# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the separate test backend (Docker project `moneo-qa`, `.env.qa`) and this checkout's app on http://localhost:3100. The config starts the app with `npm run qa:server` (or a production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless it is already running.

## Setup

1. Create the test backend once (and after pulling new migrations): `npm run setup -- --qa`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `npm run qa:auth`. Its login is stored in `.env.qa` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `npm run qa:reset`.

The whole test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` and step 1 start it fresh. The owner's `moneo` project is never touched.

Tests never use the owner's workspace. Every spec runs with the saved QA session and an `x-moneo-test` header; with that header the app refuses a request that has no valid session instead of signing the owner in (`proxy.ts`). Before any spec runs, `e2e/global-setup.ts` checks that the server under test does this, so an older or foreign server on the port stops the run.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. The QA server builds into `.next-qa`, so it can run beside `npm run dev`.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` stub or skip the backend. Against a configured backend they still need the QA session, like every spec.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `*.provider.spec.ts` call the real AI model, so they cost money. They run only with `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; `npm run test:e2e` leaves them out.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

## Pull-request CI

The `browser` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every pull request. It starts its own disposable `moneo-qa` backend on the runner (`npm run setup -- --qa`, with the same retry as the `database` job), creates the QA user (`npm run qa:auth`), builds this checkout and serves it on port 3100 against `.env.qa` with AI, bank and Scalable access off (`E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`, see `scripts/qa-server.mjs`), then runs one worker with one retry over a bounded set of specs: `net-worth.gated.spec.ts` (accepting a cash-machine proposal card once even when double-clicked, dismissing one without applying it, and checking both after a reload; proposal cards have no undo, so none is tested) and `import-journey.mocked.spec.ts`. A failure fails the job and uploads `test-results/` (a trace and screenshot per failed test) as the `browser-failures` artifact for 7 days. The runner and its backend are discarded afterwards, and the specs only create synthetic rows, so the artifact holds no owner data or credentials. The specs refuse any server that would sign tests in as the owner (`e2e/global-setup.ts`).

To reproduce a CI failure locally, follow Setup, make sure nothing else is serving port 3100, and run:

```sh
E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 npx playwright test --workers=1 e2e/net-worth.gated.spec.ts e2e/import-journey.mocked.spec.ts
npx playwright show-trace test-results/<failed test folder>/trace.zip
```

## Nightly

`npm run qa:nightly -- --install` schedules the whole suite for 03:00 every day (a Windows scheduled task that starts as soon as possible if the PC was off). It runs every spec twice on a production build of `origin/main`, in its own worktree in `~/.moneo/nightly`, and keeps one GitHub issue, "Nightly browser suite is failing", up to date. A night with Docker off or port 3100 busy is skipped quietly; the log is `~/.moneo/nightly.log`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.provider.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start `npm run qa:server` with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` (and the AI key in `.env.qa`) and run the spec with the same variable and `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.
